name: 3D realities, splats and the drone viewer
summary: Viewing a reality in 3D: Gaussian splats, point clouds, navigation controls and the drone map view. Which of these customers get, compared with support users, is the main open question.

roles.note: These modes are gated by user type and capture type, not by a permission string. Project viewing itself needs view-project (VIEW-FEAT-01).

requirements.title: A splat is shown only when a splat file exists next to the capture
requirements.statement: For video-walk captures, the viewer looks for a Gaussian splat beside the capture's images file, trying in turn splat_compressed.ply, splat.ksplat, splat.ply and the processing pipeline's point_cloud.ply. The first one found is used. 360 images, phone images and drone panoramas never get a splat. If none is found, 3D mode stays off.

requirements.title: Who can use 3D (splat) mode
requirements.statement: The PRD expects users to navigate Gaussian splat models. Today customers get the Reality and 3D buttons only on drone captures; support users get them on every capture. 3D is disabled when no splat was found.

dispute.summary: The Gaussian splat PRD addresses users generally. The code hides 3D mode from customers except on drone captures. Product must say whether splats are a customer feature (DEC-035).

requirements.title: Orbit and first-person navigation in 3D
requirements.statement: 3D views offer intuitive real-time navigation: orbit and first-person controls. Today a drone capture opens in orbit and other captures in first-person, and the BIM view has its own orbit option.

requirements.title: Compare a splat with a non-splat reality
requirements.statement: Compare mode works when one side is a Gaussian splat and the other is not, for example a splat of one date against a 360 video of another. Notes, tasks and issues stay visible in image view.
requirements.rationale: The code has a separate splat viewer for the compare side. How differences between the two kinds are handled is a PRD open question.

requirements.title: Who can switch to point cloud view
requirements.statement: The BIM navigation PRD shows a "Show point cloud" button whenever images are available. Today the point cloud mode button is shown only to support users with beta features on. A later drone PRD asked to remove the Reality/Point Cloud toggle for drone captures, which matches today's customer experience.

dispute.summary: bim-navigation FR-003 expects a point cloud button for users. The code limits it to support users behind a beta flag. The unregistered drone-viewer PRD (2024-11) asked for the toggle to be removed. Product must say whether customers get point clouds at all (DEC-035).

requirements.title: Drone captures open in a map view
requirements.statement: When a structure has a drone capture, the viewer offers a Map View of the drone orthophoto. With no sheet, the drone map is the default view (VIEW-REQ-001).
